headline: Navigating the Niagara River Corridor
reservation: No entry permit is required for the public viewing areas of the Falls. Individual attractions such as the boat tours or tunnels require separate tickets; during peak summer months, booking timed entries in advance is recommended to avoid long queues.

days.title: The Power of the Horseshoe
days.start: Suggested: 9:00 AM from Queen Victoria Park

stops.name: Table Rock Centre
stops.detail: Stand at the brink of the Horseshoe Falls to experience the immense scale and sound of the cascading water.

stops.name: Journey Behind the Falls
stops.detail: Descend via elevator to the tunnels behind the water curtain for a unique subterranean perspective.

days.driving: Allow 15–20 minutes for local parking transfers; conditions vary with pedestrian traffic.
days.note: Expect to get wet at these locations; waterproof ponchos are typically provided at the attractions.

days.title: River Gorges and Whirlpools
days.start: Suggested: 10:00 AM from the Niagara Parkway

stops.name: White Water Walk
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk alongside the Class 6 rapids of the Niagara River to see the power of the water downstream.

stops.name: Niagara Whirlpool
stops.detail: Observe the natural phenomenon where the river turns abruptly, creating a massive counter-clockwise vortex.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes along the Parkway; conditions vary by season.
days.note: The WEGO bus system is an efficient alternative to driving and parking along the river corridor.

days.title: Garden City and Historic Heights

stops.name: Niagara Glen Nature Reserve
stops.detail: Hike the rugged trails through the Carolinian forest down to the river’s edge for a quiet escape from the crowds.

stops.name: Queenston Heights Park
stops.detail: Visit the site of the historic War of 1812 battle and the Brock’s Monument overlooking the valley.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the full drive to Niagara-on-the-Lake; conditions vary with tourism volume.
days.note: Niagara Glen trails are steep and can be slippery after rain; wear appropriate footwear for rocky terrain.

intel.title: Pedestrian Flow
intel.text: The sidewalk near Table Rock becomes extremely crowded by midday. Utilize the Falls Incline Railway to move between the Fallsview hotel district and the park level easily.

intel.title: Illumination Schedule
intel.text: The Falls are lit every night, but the start time shifts throughout the year based on sunset. Check the Niagara Parks schedule for specific seasonal firework displays.

intel.title: Managed Lots
intel.text: Parking near the brink is expensive and fills early. The Rapidsview Parking Lot offers a shuttle service that is often more convenient than searching for spots in the core.

intel.title: Border Roaming
intel.text: Cellular devices often ping towers across the river in the USA. Ensure your roaming settings are configured to avoid unexpected charges while near the gorge.

intel.title: Urban Supply
intel.text: Fuel and electric charging stations are plentiful throughout the city of Niagara Falls. Prices may be slightly higher near the tourist district than in St. Catharines.

plan.arrival: Fly into Toronto Pearson and drive 90 minutes south; most visitors check in to hotels in the Fallsview district or Niagara-on-the-Lake before exploring.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for this urban-scenic mix; RVs should use designated long-term parking at the Rapidsview lot as city streets are congested.
plan.goldenHour: Oakes Garden Theatre offers a framed view of the American and Horseshoe Falls for evening photography during the summer months.
